title: introduce-cost-habitat-batcher-and-quant-thresholds
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a new batcher and quantization threshold presets that reduce token unit cost for mixed workloads; instrumentation added for SLO monitoring; safe rollback via feature flag.
description:
Context and motivation: Production tenants exhibit bimodal request sizes across chat and completion routes. Current global defaults for batching and cache expiry are conservative and underutilize opportunities for unit-cost savings. This PR introduces the 'cost-habitat' batcher (a lightweight tenant-aware batch allocator) and a set of quantization-threshold presets that automatically choose more aggressive qprofiles for stable low-sequence workloads.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds cost-habitat batcher implementation (go/runtime/batcher/cost_habitat.go) that probabilistically groups requests by observed seq-length distribution and tenant SLA tier. It prefers tight batches for latency-critical tenants and opportunistic multi-tenant packing for best-effort tiers.
- Introduces quant-threshold-presets (configs/quant_thresholds/*) with three profiles: conservative, balanced, opportunistic. Profiles are applied by default via the defaults service when tenant workload signals are stable.
- Wiring: server config flag to enable habitat batching per deployment mode; defaults service integration to recommend quant profiles; rollout guard via feature flag 'cost_habitat_enabled'.
- Observability: telemetry hooks added (metrics: habitat.batch_size, habitat.wait_ms, quant.profile_applied) and tracing tags for batch composition. Added dashboard panel definitions (observability/dashboards/habitat_cost_panels.json).

Testing and validation performed:
- Unit tests cover deterministic composition (80%+ branch coverage for allocator).
- Integration test run in perf-canary: simulated mixed workload (50% short-chat, 30% mid-completion, 20% long-generation) across 5 tenants. Observed: 13–18% token cost reduction for best-effort tier; latency SLOs met for latency tier (p95 within SLO).
- Load test (k8s perf lab): no increase in CUD memory churn; KV cache hit-rate unchanged for conservative profile.
- Canary rollout plan: gradual enable per-cluster (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated revert if quant.profile_applied correlates with >2% regression in model-quality telemetry over 1 hour.

Rollout and safety:
- Feature-flagged by default off. Operator docs include a checklist to enable per-cluster. Defaults recommender only suggests an opportunistic profile when sequence-length variance < 0.12 and prefix-stability > 0.9 over 24 hours.
- Safe fallback: if model-quality regressions detected (confidence drop or eval-set BLEU/semantic similarity degradation tied to quant profile), defaults service reverts to previous profile and the feature flag is toggled off for that tenant.

- Priya Rao: "Unit tests look good; can you add a small e2e smoke to the perf-canary harness?"
- Author: "Added perf-canary smoke scenarios; results included above."
- Jonas Meyer: "CI flaked on the first run due to a test ordering race; second run fixed by adding explicit seed. Approving after green."

CI summary: initial pipeline had flaky test failure (race), re-ran single job; final status: all checks passed (unit, integration, lint, go vet).

Migration/compatibility notes:
- No API changes for external customers. Internal defaults service behavior changes are backward compatible; operators can opt-in via feature flag. Quant presets are additive.

Why this is different from previous work: Instead of a single global batcher or purely model-driven quant selection, this patch introduces a tenant-aware, probabilistic packer combined with heuristic-driven quant thresholds. The goal is to create a small, observable decision layer that can be iterated quickly and safely, enabling measurable unit-econ improvement without heavy manual tuning.

Follow-ups and open items:

- ENG-1511: run extended quality regression sweep on opportunistic profile across additional models (including decoder-only and encoder-decoder families).
- Product asks: Add UI controls in Redwood Console to preview recommended quant profile per-tenant (tracked in ENG-1520).
